Emergency Water Damage Restoration in Reno, NV

Water damage requires immediate action across the Reno-Tahoe region, and the area's extreme climate range creates risks unlike anywhere else in the West. Sierra Nevada winters push temperatures well below freezing across Washoe County and the Tahoe basin, bursting pipes in older Reno homes and vacation properties that sit unoccupied for weeks at a time. Spring snowmelt sends the Truckee River surging through downtown Reno, threatening properties along its banks and overwhelming stormwater systems across Sparks and the valley floor. In the Tahoe basin, elevation-driven temperature swings create freeze-thaw cycles that stress roofing, flashing, and plumbing in ways that flat-terrain properties never experience.

The region's housing stock amplifies these risks. Downtown Reno and Midtown carry significant inventory of older buildings with aging plumbing. Lake Tahoe vacation rentals often sit unheated and unwatched during off-season cold snaps -- exactly the conditions that produce catastrophic pipe failures. And the region's growing suburban communities in Spanish Springs and Cold Springs face flash flooding from the high desert's intense but infrequent rainfall events. Our team responds 24/7 throughout Washoe County, Carson City, and the entire Lake Tahoe basin.

Water Damage Restoration Services

  • Inspection and damage assessment
  • Water extraction with industrial pumps
  • Structural drying and dehumidification
  • Cleaning and sanitization
  • Restoration and repairs

Common Causes of Water Damage in Reno-Tahoe

  • Burst pipes from Sierra Nevada freezing temperatures
  • Truckee River flooding and spring snowmelt
  • Roof leaks and ice dams at Lake Tahoe elevations
  • Unoccupied vacation property pipe failures during cold snaps
  • Flash flooding in high-desert Reno valleys
  • Water heater and appliance failures

Emergency Fire Damage Restoration in Reno, NV

After a fire, you need complete restoration that goes beyond basic cleanup. 911 Restoration of Reno provides full-service fire damage restoration throughout Reno-Sparks, Carson City, and Lake Tahoe communities. From smoke and soot removal to structural repairs and content cleaning, we understand the emotional toll of fire loss and work with compassion and efficiency to restore your property.

The Reno-Tahoe region's fire risk is among the highest in the nation. Wildfire smoke from regional fires causes widespread smoke damage to properties across Washoe County even when structures are never directly threatened -- penetrating HVAC systems, depositing soot on surfaces, and leaving persistent odor that requires professional-grade treatment. In the Tahoe basin, the combination of dry summers, high winds, and dense forest creates structure fire risk that demands restoration teams experienced with high-altitude, timber-frame, and log construction. Our team is trained for the full range of property types found throughout Northern Nevada.

Mold Remediation & Removal in Reno-Tahoe

Mold can develop within 24 to 48 hours of water exposure in Reno-Tahoe properties, posing serious health risks and causing structural damage. Our certified mold remediation specialists safely remove mold and address the moisture source to prevent recurrence. The Reno-Tahoe region's dual climate identity -- arid high-desert on the valley floor and moisture-laden alpine environment at lake level -- creates mold risk profiles that vary dramatically by location and property type.

In the Tahoe basin, lakeside humidity, snowmelt intrusion, and the freeze-thaw cycles common in Incline Village, Kings Beach, and Tahoe City properties create persistent moisture conditions in crawlspaces, basements, and wall cavities. Across the Reno-Sparks valley floor, water damage from plumbing failures and storm events in older housing stock can trigger mold growth that goes undetected for months, particularly in properties that sit vacant during summer. We handle mold issues common to both high-desert Reno homes and alpine Lake Tahoe properties throughout Washoe County.

Mold Remediation Services

  • Professional inspection and testing
  • Containment to prevent spore spread
  • HEPA filtration and air scrubbing
  • Safe removal and antimicrobial treatment
  • Moisture source identification and repair

Signs Your Property Needs Mold Remediation

  • Musty or earthy odors in any room or enclosed space
  • Visible mold growth on surfaces
  • Recent water damage or flooding
  • Allergy or respiratory symptoms that worsen indoors
  • Discoloration or staining on walls or ceilings

Sewage Cleanup in Reno-Tahoe

Sewage backups are hazardous emergencies requiring immediate professional attention. Raw sewage contains dangerous bacteria, viruses, and parasites that pose serious health risks to families and employees. Aging sewer infrastructure in downtown Reno and the older inner Sparks neighborhoods creates backup risk during heavy rainfall events. In rural Washoe Valley and the outlying communities of Lyon and Douglas counties, private septic systems face failure risk particularly during wet winters and spring snowmelt when drain fields become saturated. Our team responds 24/7 to sewage emergencies throughout Washoe County and the Lake Tahoe region.

Sewage Cleanup Process

  • Emergency sewage extraction
  • Contaminated material removal
  • Professional-grade sanitization
  • Odor removal treatment
  • Structural drying and restoration

Health Threats We Address

  • E. coli and other bacteria
  • Hepatitis and viral pathogens
  • Parasites and protozoa
  • Toxic gases and fumes
  • Secondary mold growth
⚠️ Warning: Never attempt sewage cleanup yourself. Contact our 24/7 emergency line immediately at (775) 239-3690 for safe, professional cleanup.

Storm & Disaster Damage Restoration in Reno-Tahoe

Sierra Nevada storms bring challenges to Reno-Tahoe properties that don't exist at lower elevations. Heavy snowfall collapses roofs in Incline Village and throughout the Tahoe basin. Ice dams force snowmelt under roofing and into wall cavities, causing damage that often doesn't surface until spring thaw. Atmospheric rivers deliver days of continuous rainfall that overwhelms drainage and sends the Truckee River into Reno neighborhoods. And regional wildfires -- whether actively threatening structures or burning many miles away -- leave smoke damage and air quality impacts that require professional remediation across the entire region. 911 Restoration of Reno responds immediately when any of these events strikes, day or night.

Frequently Asked Reno-Tahoe Emergency Restoration Questions

How quickly can you respond to a water damage emergency in the Reno-Tahoe area?
Our restoration team typically arrives within 45 minutes of your call throughout Washoe County. We're available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays. Call (775) 239-3690 for immediate assistance.
Does 911 Restoration of Reno work with insurance companies?
Yes. We work directly with all major insurance carriers and handle the claims process on your behalf. Our team documents damage thoroughly and bills your insurance company directly, minimizing your out-of-pocket costs.
How long does water damage restoration take in Reno-Tahoe?
Most residential water damage restoration projects take 3 to 5 days depending on the extent of damage. The Tahoe basin's higher humidity can extend drying times compared to the drier Reno valley floor, and our team accounts for that on every project. We provide a detailed timeline after our initial on-site assessment.
What should I do while waiting for your team to arrive?
If it is safe to do so, turn off the water source, move valuables to dry areas, and avoid walking through standing water near electrical outlets or appliances. Do not use household vacuums on standing water, and do not attempt mold removal yourself. Our team will handle everything when we arrive.
What Reno-Tahoe areas do you serve?
We serve Reno, Sparks, Sun Valley, Cold Springs, Spanish Springs, Verdi, Lemmon Valley, Washoe Valley, and surrounding Washoe County communities; Carson City; Douglas County communities including Minden, Gardnerville, Stateline, and Zephyr Cove; Lyon County communities including Dayton and Fernley; and Lake Tahoe basin communities including South Lake Tahoe, Tahoe City, Kings Beach, Incline Village, Crystal Bay, Carnelian Bay, Tahoe Vista, Truckee, and Glenbrook.
